title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1967-01-27

ai_review.summary: High‑energy ’67 show with a scorching Viola Lee Blues, but the sped‑up audience tape sounds chipmunk‑like and often unlistenable.
ai_review.review: The performance captures an intense early‑Dead set – frantic Viola Lee Blues, powerful Pigpen vocals and raw urgency that many fans love. Unfortunately the source is a fast‑forwarded audience recording, giving high‑pitched, almost unintelligible vocals and burying Phil’s bass, so the listening experience suffers unless the tape is slowed down.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is praised (high energy, standout jams) while recording quality is widely criticized for speed and pitch issues; the weighted average yields a solid‑mid rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Tape is sped up causing chipmunk‑like vocals, high‑pitched Jerry and Pigpen, loss of Phil's bass depth; occasional clarity improvements over other sources but overall muddy and difficult to listen to without pitch correction.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Reviewers note the song order is wrong and the set list appears butchered, but the music itself flows with frantic intensity.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His voice sounds high‑pitched due to speed; some reviewers still praise his primal guitar work.
band_member_comments.Phil: Deep bass often gets lost in the sped‑up recording, though his playing is noted as solid when audible.
